content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (Section 10.3, ¶p0063).**

- **What the document says:** Section 10.3 is a bare "binding upon successors and assigns" provision with no consent standard, no affiliate/M&A carve-out, and no restriction on either party's transfer.
- **Direction check:** There is no change-of-control language anywhere in the Agreement, and no HDI termination or re-pricing right triggered by a change of control of the Company — so the walk-away scenario does not arise, and our own assignment freedom is unrestricted (better than preferred for us).
- **Why it still fails the fallback:** The permissive silence cuts both ways — HDI could assign the hosting/development engagement to any third party, including a competitor of ours, without consent or notice. The fallback requires a consent standard for non-successor assignments.
- **Redline (preferred, validated ok:true):** Appended to 10.3 an express Company right to assign to an affiliate or merger/asset-sale successor without consent, plus a requirement that HDI obtain our prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never assign to a Company competitor.
